source: Hand-compiled from public cable maps and news reports (rounded; TeleGeography, operators)
caveat: A sample of the main corridors with simplified routes, not the exact seabed paths. Hundreds of cables exist.
facts: Roughly 95% or more of the world's international data travels through undersea cables, not satellites.
Cables are about as thick as a garden hose. Most faults are caused by ship anchors and fishing, not attacks.
Cable systems cluster through a few chokepoints: the Red Sea and Egypt, the Strait of Malacca, the Channel and the Baltic.

cables.note: Virginia Beach to Bilbao. Built by Microsoft, Meta and Telxius; one of the highest-capacity cables across the Atlantic.
New York to the UK and Spain. Google's cable.
Virginia Beach to the French Atlantic coast. Google's cable.
Oregon to Japan, across the north Pacific. Google and Asian partners.
California to Japan and the Philippines. Amazon, Meta and Asian partners.
Sydney to New Zealand, Fiji, Hawaii and California.
Singapore to France via India, the Gulf, the Red Sea and Egypt: a main route between Asia and Europe.
Loops round Africa from Europe to the Gulf, led by Meta. One of the longest cable systems ever built.
Florida to Brazil. Google and partners.
Finland to Germany across the Baltic. Damaged in November 2024.

hubs.note: Europe's gateway for cables from Asia and Africa, with a major data-centre cluster.
Where several of the biggest Atlantic cables come ashore.
The main hub of Southeast Asia, where cables from Asia, Europe and Australia meet.
Most cables between Asia and Europe pass through Egypt, a major chokepoint.
Cables from the Gulf and India land here.
A key hub for China and the region.
Where Pacific cables from Asia and Australia land.
The world's biggest data-centre cluster; a large part of internet traffic passes through.
Europe's cloud hub, with strained power supply.
Home of the world's biggest internet exchange.
Asia's biggest cloud and exchange hub together with Singapore.
The largest cloud markets in China.

incidents.note: A volcanic eruption cut the only cable to the islands, taking the country offline for weeks.
Two cables linking Taiwan's Matsu islands were damaged; Taiwan suspected ships from China.
Several cables were damaged after a ship hit by Houthi missiles sank and dragged its anchor, hitting traffic between Asia and Europe.
Two cables were cut. Investigators suspected a ship's dragged anchor; no intent was established.
The Estlink 2 power cable and several data cables were damaged; Finland detained a ship.
